attribution.note: Zitron's own argument in his newsletter, put in his own words.

semantics.note: Keeps the causal claim (timelines, not only power) and the counterfactual reasoning. 'Clearly' is firm, so this is not hedged.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair. It does not deny that power matters, and it requires project-level evidence of the cause. The affected population and how strong the effect must be are left unspecified, which is correctly flagged.

evidence.note: Sightline shows little construction progress against 2026 targets. It does not say whether construction schedules or power caused the shortfall.
JLL reports grid lead times over four years, a competing explanation. Its common construction delays and equipment lead times do not show that schedules were infeasible.

reviews.rationale: No matched project records separate infeasible construction schedules from delays caused by power, and no count of finished but unpowered sites tests the counterfactual. The packet gives industry-wide context pointing both ways, but neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion, which he partly bases on an unnamed source.

semantics.note: Keeps the broad scope ('everybody', 'as much as possible') and all three parts of the claim.

contract.note: An ordinary reading of plural 'hyperscalers' and of token-based pay. Counting work that engineers later repair as reaching production matches the speaker's own context. A March 2026 window is a reasonable choice.

evidence.note: Meta made AI use part of its reviews in 2026. This is not tied to token volume and covers one firm.
A June 2025 Microsoft memo making AI use mandatory. This falls outside the target period and does not tie anything to tokens.
A September 2026 Meta denial alongside employee accounts of tokenmaxxing. This is later and does not settle what the March policy was.
In March, Meta told designers to try coding and used token dashboards. It does not show pay tied to tokens, production releases, or other hyperscalers.

reviews.rationale: Partial pieces appear at Meta (AI use in reviews, token dashboards, designers told to code), but nothing shows pay tied to token volume, features reaching production, or the scope across hyperscalers in March 2026. Meta's later denial does not settle the policy either. Neither condition is met.

semantics.note: 'Mostly sitting waiting' is fairly read as most of the value being uninstalled. The surrounding text supports treating these as NVIDIA GPUs.

contract.note: Reading 'mostly' as more than half by sales value is ordinary. The cohort start date and geography are undefined but flagged, and the observation window before the post is reasonable.

evidence.note: The NVIDIA filing says headquarters-based revenue geography is not where chips ship. It does not measure installation.
Nadella says Microsoft has chips it cannot plug in. This shows a bottleneck at one firm, with no share of value.
CBRE data on Northern Virginia absorption. This covers one regional market and says nothing about GPU installation value.

reviews.rationale: No source matches GPU sales value to installation status. The evidence shows a bottleneck exists at Microsoft and gives regional data center context, but nothing shows whether more or less than half of sales value was uninstalled.

attribution.note: The 'largest wastes' line paraphrases JustDario but is adopted as Zitron's own. 'I anticipate' the majority never get built is his own words.

semantics.note: 'I anticipate' is unqualified expectation, so this is a forecast. The 'largest waste of capital' part has no measure and cannot be scored on its own, which the contract notes.

contract.note: Counting distinct deals and requiring permanent failure is fair to 'never get built'. The population of deals is undefined, which is correctly flagged.

evidence.note: Crusoe's own disclosure that Abilene's first phase is live. One partial completion does not settle the overall rate.
An April 2026 report of one cancelled project (Digital Gateway), with possible relocation. No population or failure rate is given.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The early-resolution rule needs a fixed population whose completions or permanent failures cross half, and the evidence offers only isolated examples. The capital-waste ranking cannot be measured.
